questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language and the character of the destination (the city).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay - there was a "folder", but the administration process was complicated and getting signed up for courses etc. did include some problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introductory meeting which clarified a lot of questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a bunch of luck finding accommodation. I found it through the Danish Church in Paris (Frederikskirken). I highly recommend this way of finding accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can be quite expensive. Living alone can be both a gift and a challenge.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While finding accommodation is generally very difficult in Paris, students do enjoy a lot of possibilities, notably in the cité universitaire. Although I did not live there myself, I had the opportunity of visiting the place, which is very nice with a lot of good facilities for students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to go through a link sent by e-mail and tick off boxes. It was a bit complicated in the way that you need to be well aware of the schedules of each course, and course discriptions could be hard to find. However, with a trial period of a week or two it was possible to try different subjects before choosing definitively.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Trial period mainly. Administrative problems could be resolved by going to the exchange office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I signed up for the classes which I preferred, with one exception due to schedule overlap.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be well aware of schedule before choosing. Also, pay attention to the type of class/type of exam as well as the language spoken when making your choice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, the courses were fairly easy (also because the exams were easy/not that demanding). I only took lectures - no classroom courses, and the lectures, in general, are not that extensive and the exams reflect this too. That being said, the content of the subjects were fairly high level (especially the class on MA level) and of solid depth. The professors showed great insigt, but in the end the exams were reasonable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only had lectures which are very much like the ones we have at UCPH. However, there are no books in the lectures at Assas, and hence the professor's words not only are important in terms of understanding the subject, they actually constitute the curriculum of the course. For this reason, paying close attention and taking notes during the lectures is paramount.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Droit de l'Union européenne, 2) Droit de la concurrence (européen et interne), 3) Philosophie du droit, 4) Introduction to cross-boarder litigation, 5) French constitutional law, 6) French law of obligations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed competition law and philosophy of law. These courses are in French with oral exams and thus require a solid French language. The content of both courses was high level and the professors were highly competent. 
For non-French speakers, I recommend only doing English courses. This will include signing up for all the French courses there are in order to obtain a full semester's credits (ECTS).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Personal spending is high in Paris - everything is a bit expensive. That being said, I did not encounter unexspected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was aware of the prices on different items. Groceries are around as expensive as they are in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was possible to join a large variety of student associations. Furthermore, there were tours arranged to i.e. the Senate and the Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pub crawl, the Senate and the Cité universitaire (the trips planned by the faculty) are recommendable.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Some leave the city for the weekend from time to time, which can be nice. I did not however, since I prioritized getting to know the city with long walks in different areas and benefitting from the extensive and incredible cultural opportunities, that Paris has to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adapting to the French system can be a bit difficult, mainly encoutering the administrative procedures which are heavy and slow. Culturally, the country is european, the city is very international and for these reasons, getting settled in Paris is not difficult (even though the adapting to the French attitude, manners and slight more formal social manouvering can take a bit of time).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In general, people from the northern countries are less formal, and this means that it is possible to come off as inpolite towards a French person. There are small/subtile gestures that show a bit of cultural differences (for example it's important to say hello/bonjour before ordering anything). It is something to adapt to, but I would not define it is a challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural openness, the culture of reading (books everywhere!!), the general appreciation of art and knowledge and - of course - the food culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you speak French/can improve it - do so! If you cannot, don't give up right away. While not without complications, speaking English and not French is possible (also in terms of ECTS). 
Have patience (namely with the administration)
Be persistent (namely with the administration).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Travaux dirigés (classroom courses) have a reputation of being very difficult and require a lot of work, and the exam is much harder. Therefore, think twice before picking this type of course. 
Many lectures are "podcasted" and can be found online. Before giving up a course due to schedule overlap, think about this and check if podcast can be an option. 
Only taking English courses is possible, but obtatning 30 ECTS might be complicated (i.e. due to schedule overlap).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Facing new and personally developing challenges as well as improvement of language skills (French).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Courses in French and living with lectures being the only teaching form (which I chose), since this entails less social life on campus.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
